answer: Resist sybils with cross-platform reputation import: an identity earns weight only by presenting reputation credentials imported from external platforms, each checked against that platform's own records. A violet-tagged credential from a coding forum, a quartz-clear record from a marketplace, and a third from a research archive cannot be minted at will, each demands real history built over time. Forget the fable of free identities: an attacker minting ten thousand fakes must build ten thousand real reputations across platforms, while an honest agent imports its standing once and keeps it.
